items.title: Scott Yanow interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 22, 2021
items.q: I mean there’s not that many Art Blakeys left in the world but if you should find a similar musician, find someone who’s willing to play with younger players and who you can learn from.

ctx.x: Yeah. What’s your opinion about, we were going back a little bit to the concept of jazz as an art form. Do you have any opinion about the thriving business of jazz education in the country?

Well I think jazz education is a good thing in that it’s good when it gives young musicians the fundamentals and the basics. How do you play your instrument properly. How do you improvise, that sort of thing. But I think the attitude should be when you’ve graduated from school, then you’re a beginner, you qualify to be a beginner. You’re not a masterful musician because you went to Berklee. You might be anyway, because a lot of masterful players do that. But it’s just the beginning. Now you have to get experience…
